name: permit-tracker-permit-types
title: Permit types
description: A library of the permit types: each one’s governing law and application needs, and every agency that issues it with its time to issue and past permits. Critical Areas Review links to each city’s and county’s ordinance online, with how review works and the wetland and stream buffer tables, read from the code for five southwest Washington jurisdictions. Rules are suggested by AI, edited and validated by a person, each section badged with its status and history; the Agencies grid flags jurisdictions whose ordinance changed after review, and Check for updates re-reads the code sites. Governing law is editable.

guide.intent: How long each permit type has taken at each agency, learned from every issued permit: past permits, typical (median) days, review rounds and the fastest-to-slowest range. A row opens that type at that agency.
decisions: On the Critical Areas Review page the grid becomes the statewide list: every county and city with its county, ordinance (links to the code site), last amendment, and a Rules column (AI suggested / Edited / Validated / Not read, plus Ordinance changed). Facets: Type, County, Rules, Past permits.

Ordinance changed compares the ordinance's last amendment with the date the rules were last suggested, edited or validated (a year-only date counts as Jan 1). Check for updates re-reads every code site and stamps when it ran.

On an agency's Critical Areas Review page, How review works and the wetland and stream buffers are each a card with its status badge, a history line (suggested by AI, edited by, validated by, with dates), Edit (every text, citation and table value) and Validate. The AI suggestion is kept beside any edit; Restore AI suggestion puts it back.
Governing law is editable per permit type (citation, name, link); on an agency page the local ordinance's chapter and link are editable too.
gotchas: Every citation links to the code section online and opens in a new tab; keep the citations with the text they support so a person can check one against the other.
Example rules exist only so the sample agencies have something to show; they must stay badged so nobody takes them for the agency's code.
acceptance: Sorting the Critical Areas Review grid by Rules puts jurisdictions with a changed ordinance first.
After Validate, the section's badge reads Validated and the history line names who validated it and when.
